configure.contract:
# Gate60 static configure contract

The command in PROJECTION_A.txt is a specification only. No configure, compilation or installation is authorized here. M5 must resolve the path placeholders without changing arguments or feature semantics.

## Inputs and feature selection

FLAG_PROVENANCE_LEDGER.json contains exactly 25 arguments, sorted by unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Every argument is emitted once. EXTENSION_COVERAGE.json maps all 27 M1 models: 21 explicitly selected static extensions and six unconditional built-ins. Static PHP extensions may depend on shared system libraries; static extension selection does not mean a fully static executable.

`--disable-all` suppresses optional extensions otherwise enabled by default, avoiding unrequired features such as SimpleXML/readline/sqlite3. PHP's PHP_REAL_ARG_ENABLE/WITH macros apply PHP_ENABLE_ALL only in the absence of an explicit option. Every required optional extension is therefore explicitly enabled. PDO and pdo_sqlite are explicitly restored; their default-following behavior alone would be insufficient with disable-all. Options have no shared modifier, so PHP_ARG_ANALYZE_EX selects static linkage. Internal lexbor and bundled PCRE2 remain PHP source components; they are not new Ubuntu libraries or added project requirements.

CGI and phpdbg are disabled because only the CLI SAPI is required and these default-on SAPIs are evaluated before the all-extensions switch. CLI remains enabled by its positively documented default (extension-or-not=no). No FPM, Apache, debug, optimization, coverage, sanitizer, PEAR or convenience option is introduced. PEAR is already off. mbregex stays at its default yes because it is not governed as an extension by PHP_ENABLE_ALL; its Oniguruma dependency is retained. Integrated PHP 8.5 opcache/default JIT semantics are not tuned. ZIP/libzip is NOT_REQUIRED by M1/M3; no ZIP flag is added.

M2 contributes zero configure arguments: its ini file, PHPRC, PHP_INI_SCAN_DIR, process functions and temporary-directory requirements apply at runtime. The model does not override or weaken them. The six built-ins (hash, json, pcre, date, SPL, standard), CLI default, mbregex default and integrated opcache behavior are documented from the retained/fetched PHP 8.5.8 metadata. The required default-capability count in the report is six M1 built-ins plus CLI plus mbregex (eight); integrated opcache is preserved implementation behavior, not a new M1 requirement.

The thirteen external dependency-bearing extension rows retain the exact M3 package mappings. Ten unique pkg-config identities retain the qualified version rules. Iconv uses Ubuntu glibc from libc6-dev, with no separate libiconv. intl uses qualified g++/ICU; PDO_PGSQL uses libpq; PDO_SQLite uses system SQLite. XML-family dependencies converge on the same qualified libxml2 installation. No extra library is inferred.

## Paths and shell boundaries

The future caller must resolve PHP_SOURCE_ROOT to the verified extracted PHP 8.5.8 source and PHP_INSTALL_PREFIX to an absolute qualification-owned isolated directory outside `/usr`, `/usr/local`, the repository and Packaging output. Paths must be canonical, nonempty, free of control characters and symlink escapes, and source/build/install paths must be distinct. The prefix is a deterministic placeholder; its location belongs to M5, not to M4. M5 must provide a fresh separate build working directory and verify no config.cache/config.status reuse. No local Windows path is embedded in the portable command.

The retained Ubuntu shell invokes `/bin/sh` explicitly. Double-quoted `${PHP_SOURCE_ROOT}/configure` and `--prefix=${PHP_INSTALL_PREFIX}` each remain one argument even with spaces; shell expansion does not re-evaluate metacharacters contained in variable values. Do not use eval, command-string interpolation or a second shell parse. All other fixed arguments have no whitespace or substitutions. Prefix/source validation and the authoritative argv inventory are mandatory before any future invocation.

## Configure environment

`/usr/bin/env -i` discards ambient environment variables. The command supplies only PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, LC_ALL=C, TZ=UTC, CONFIG_SITE=/dev/null, CC=/usr/bin/gcc, CXX=/usr/bin/g++, PKG_CONFIG=/usr/bin/pkg-config and the standard Ubuntu amd64 pkg-config directories. M5 resolves the path placeholders in the outer caller before env clears its environment. No inherited CFLAGS, CPPFLAGS, CXXFLAGS, LDFLAGS, LIBS, CPATH, LIBRARY_PATH, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, LD_PRELOAD, PKG_CONFIG_PATH, per-library *_CFLAGS/*_LIBS, shell startup variables, CONFIG_SITE or cached ac_cv_* values may enter configure. The canonical command introduces no custom compiler/linker optimization flags; PHP's exact-version defaults remain in force.

PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR is explicitly limited to `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/pkgconfig:/usr/lib/pkgconfig:/usr/share/pkgconfig`, the qualified standard system metadata locations. This is not a custom external library path. No PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR, /usr/local metadata, private library installation or fallback is admitted. Before future configure, require all ten M3 pkg-config identities and constraints from those authenticated package installations, and verify emitted include/library paths resolve to qualified system/bundled dependencies. Compiler/tool/default include paths and selected library headers must not shadow these with an undeclared /usr/local or user installation. Unknown resolution, unqualified tool ownership, missing metadata, version mismatch or undeclared library fails the future preflight; do not add packages or flags dynamically.

The model's zero uncontrolled-environment and ambient-dependency counts describe the explicit admission policy and fully declared dependencies, not a measured future runner state. Actual compiler/system probing and configure success remain NOT_EXECUTED. Gate59 apt trust observation/authentication must precede any installation of the declared dependencies. Historical apt trust remains unproven and is not used.

## Static qualification and M5 handoff

The positive and ten negative fixtures validate the same ledger, rejecting unknown/missing/conflicting flags, undeclared/wrong dependencies, failed version rules, nonisolated prefix, convenience flags, Windows paths and ambient inputs. Projection A reads the generated provenance ledger; B independently reconstructs choices from immutable M1 and the reviewed core/prefix rules. Both use the same canonical rendering convention, and neither copies the other's output. Byte equality is recorded in PROJECTION_RESULT.json.

The unchanged M1 capabilities preserve Composer 2.9.4 and recovered project platform requirements statically. No required process function is disabled and M2 ini behavior remains unchanged. M5 must still verify actual extension loading, runtime library linkage, ini selection, exact PHP version and platform compatibility after a separately authorized build. This gate does not close M5 or certify Hosted execution.

prospective_apt_trust_guard:
# Gate59 prospective apt trust contract

This contract applies only to future PHP qualification. It does not certify a runner, authorize execution, establish historical apt trust, or replace Gate58's failure. M3 can be complete as a future qualification model while the future observation result remains NOT_EXECUTED.

## Observation and ordering

The future implementation must complete these phases serially. No package-manager command runs in Gate59.

1. In the eventual qualification runner, record runner name, OS, architecture, agent version, image name/version, image release when exposed, and `/etc/os-release`. Require Ubuntu ID=ubuntu, VERSION_ID=24.04, VERSION_CODENAME=noble and dpkg architecture amd64; runner architecture must agree as X64. Missing mandatory identity fields, tools or observation commands fail. Image release may be explicitly NOT_EXPOSED. Do not accept ubuntu-latest as an observed OS identity.
2. Read effective apt configuration with the eventual command environment accounted for, including APT_CONFIG, configuration fragments, source-list/sourceparts and trusted/trustedparts paths. Record hashes and relevant settings, not arbitrary raw environment values. Require default governed source/config paths; reject alternate roots, nonstandard source directories, unknown acquisition/proxy hooks, executable pre/post hooks, and unresolved options. Capture all source files, including disabled definitions, and referenced mirror lists and public keyrings. No apt update, install or download is allowed in this phase.
3. Normalize and validate every source and trust reference using the rules below. Reject any active third-party source, even if apparently unrelated to the canonical package set. Gate59 deliberately does not permit the optional unrelated-third-party exception. Disabled sources are recorded but cannot supply packages. No automatic disabling, deletion or rewriting of sources is authorized: a runner outside the policy stops.
4. Bind all 30 unique Gate55 direct packages to enabled Noble amd64 official source tuples and retained component requirements. Require exactly the canonical set, no missing/extra direct packages, and at least one enabled noble/main binary source. This is pre-refresh policy/intention binding, not a claim to know fresh candidate versions. No cached package index may establish trust. With all active sources official and no alternate apt configuration, no third-party candidate source is admissible. Any unresolved binding fails before the first apt mutation.
5. Emit preinstall evidence and a PASS decision. Seal hashes of sources, config, mirror files, keyrings, package inventory and command policy. Re-read immediately before refresh and installation; any change fails. Use a controlled environment and single sequential process on a trusted isolated ephemeral runner; concurrent configuration writers invalidate the observation. This assumes the Hosted OS/tooling execution boundary, not an adversarial kernel.
6. Only a separately authorized future execution gate may now run an authenticated index refresh. Do not reuse stale lists after any refresh error, warning of insecure or unauthenticated metadata, expired metadata, suite/origin change, or partial failure. Treat any repository failure as fatal; no fallback, retry, allow-releaseinfo-change, or insecure override. Verify actual Release Origin=Ubuntu, suite/codename against the admitted Noble suite set, signatures against admitted archive keys, and fresh authenticated index hashes. The governing execution must retain apt authentication diagnostics and reject unrecognized signing identities.
7. Before package installation, resolve all canonical candidates from those authenticated indexes. Check origin, suite, component, architecture (amd64 or architecture-independent all), retained library constraints and artifact filename/hash binding. Reject third-party installed versions that would be silently kept as satisfying a requested dependency. Simulate the exact transaction and record its dependency closure. Only the 30 canonical packages are direct requests; necessary transitive dependencies guaranteed by Ubuntu package metadata are permitted, not opportunistic additions. Every dependency must have the same official authenticated provenance. Reject removals, unauthenticated artifacts, unexpected source changes and unresolved constraints. Install the recorded approved versioned transaction without recommends or unauthenticated options; if the plan changes, stop. Normal apt artifact hash verification remains mandatory. These are future actions, not Gate59 actions.

## Deterministic source normalization

Read files in bytewise pathname order; reject unreadable, oversized, NUL-containing, invalid-UTF8, unexpected extension/type, ambiguous symlink or non-root-writable-by-others configuration. Bound observation to 128 files, 1 MiB per file, 8 MiB total; overflow fails. Resolve approved file symlinks and capture both link and target identities. Unknown active source syntax fails.

For `.list`, ignore blank/comment-only lines and strip trailing comments only outside brackets. Parse `deb` or `deb-src`, optional bracketed key=value options, URI, suite, then components. Reject duplicate/conflicting options, unsupported substitutions, flat repositories and unknown options. For deb822 `.sources`, parse blank-line-separated stanzas, case-insensitive field names, continuation lines and full-line comments. Reject duplicate fields, malformed continuation, embedded key material and unknown fields affecting trust/selection. `Enabled: no` disables a stanza; absent or yes enables it; other values fail. Expand Types x URIs x Suites, tokenize Components/Architectures/Signed-By and retain source-file/stanza provenance. Canonical records sort/deduplicate identical tuples; incompatible duplicate trust settings fail. `deb-src` is observed and must meet the same provenance rules but does not bind binary packages.

Normalize URI scheme/host to lowercase, default port only, and one trailing slash; reject userinfo, query, fragment, percent-encoded ambiguity, path traversal, nonstandard ports and unapproved redirects. Accept only http/https `archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/`, `security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/`, and `azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/`. HTTP is admissible only because archive signatures/index hashes remain mandatory; TLS verification may never be disabled for HTTPS. No broad hostname suffix or mirror wildcard.

Accept `mirror+file:/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt` only after reading that bounded root-controlled local file: every nonblank mirror entry must normalize to an allowed URI; only unique numeric priority metadata is allowed. Reject nested, remote or unknown mirror-list forms. Record the expanded endpoints and file hash. No source rewrite is performed.

Admit suites noble, noble-updates and noble-security; require noble coverage for the retained package baseline. Other suites, including proposed/backports or other releases, fail rather than infer compatibility. Components may be main, restricted, universe, multiverse, but each required package must match its retained Gate55 component. Architectures absent means observed system architecture; otherwise the effective list must include amd64 and contain no unresolved add/remove modifiers. Reject architectures other than amd64/all in package candidates.

## Trust and authentication

Explicit Signed-By must resolve to readable public keyring file paths, with optional full fingerprints selecting keys; no inline keys, short IDs, remote keys or missing paths. Verify regular-file ownership/permissions and key provenance via the installed Ubuntu keyring package inventory plus full public-key fingerprints. For implicit trust, enumerate every effective system trusted keyring. Implicit trust is admitted only when every effective signer is an approved Ubuntu archive signer; unrelated global keys cause failure. Never infer apt-key use, and never export private keys.

The admitted archive key for this bounded policy is the Ubuntu Archive Automatic Signing Key (2018), full fingerprint `F6ECB3762474EDA9D21B7022871920D1991BC93C`, corroborated by official Ubuntu documentation. Additional effective signers require separately reviewed authority; key rotation causes a closed failure, not automatic trust expansion. For multi-key files, every effective key must be admitted, or an explicit Signed-By full fingerprint must limit the effective set. File existence or package ownership alone is not sufficient. Never derive an expected fingerprint or checksum from the same artifact being verified.

Reject effective global, host-specific and per-source authentication bypasses: APT::Get::AllowUnauthenticated, Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories, AllowWeakRepositories, AllowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories, trusted=yes, allow-insecure=yes, allow-weak=yes, signature disabling, disabled Check-Date/Check-Valid-Until, or disabled HTTPS Verify-Peer/Verify-Host. Future command-line flags and environment must not override these settings. Reject unknown trust-affecting options. A missing Signed-By is not assumed insecure by itself; it must pass the strict implicit-trust policy above.

Official apt semantics bind signed Release/InRelease metadata to Packages indexes and package artifact hashes. That describes the future mechanism only; successful actual observation and authentication remain required.

## Evidence, failure and limits

Write a bounded JSON evidence artifact under the future qualification evidence directory, outside source and Packaging output. Include contract/inventory hashes, timestamps, runner/OS identity, normalized source tuples with enabled state, referenced public keyring paths/fingerprints, authentication decisions, 30 intended bindings, phase-specific actual authentication/candidate results, exit status and first failed rule. Mark future-only fields NOT_EXECUTED until observed. Cap artifact size at 10 MiB and fail on overflow.

Do not dump apt credentials, auth.conf, proxy passwords, environment secrets or raw private keys. Detect URI userinfo and secret-bearing configuration, record only a safe rejection class, and stop; do not serialize the value. Public fingerprints and approved paths may be retained. Keep raw source content out of the artifact; normalized allowlisted fields and hashes suffice.

Unknown, malformed, missing, internal-error or conflicting evidence always fails; no fix-and-continue, source removal, new repository, fallback, retry or package expansion. A future runner with active Microsoft or other non-Ubuntu sources can fail this conservative policy even when unrelated packages appear harmless. Such failure does not invalidate the completeness of the prospective model or establish future runner admissibility. It requires a later authority decision.

References: Gate55 canonical package ledger and existing dependency constraints; [Ubuntu archive verification](https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/software-integrity/archive-verification/); [Ubuntu signing-key documentation](https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/software-integrity/image-verification/). These explain prospective trust semantics, not historical image contents.

safety_and_cleanup.contract:
# Gate61 isolated installation/runtime contract

This is a static specification only. No source/runtime download, configure, compilation, installation, apt action or Hosted execution is performed. M1–M4 remain immutable inputs. Start-gate readiness requires the complete static specification and a separate execution decision.

## Layout

Let Q be canonical `${RUNNER_TEMP}/appart-php858-qualification-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}`. Require numeric run identifiers, an absolute canonical runner-owned temporary root, and a new nonexisting Q. Refuse reuse rather than deleting a previous campaign. Q must be outside the repository and Packaging output; reject symlinks, overlap, path traversal and unsafe ownership. Record its resolved path once.

Use these pairwise separate children: `downloads`, `source/php-8.5.8`, `build`, `php`, `composer`, `configuration`, `configuration/empty-scan`, `tmp`, `home`, `composer-home`, `composer-cache`, `evidence`. Composer artifact is Q/composer/composer-2.9.4.phar; wrapper is Q/composer/bin/composer; PHP executable is Q/php/bin/php; ini is Q/configuration/php.ini. No source/build/install/Composer artifact enters the repository or Packaging inventory. The configuration subtree intentionally contains the empty scan directory; the required source/build/install/Composer roots are disjoint siblings.

## Exact inputs and build/install model

Only after the future runner satisfies Gate59 preinstall apt policy may a separately authorized execution install the exact Gate55 direct package set and its authenticated necessary transitive dependencies. No automatic source cleanup or repository enablement is permitted.

The future PHP source archive is https://www.php.net/distributions/php-8.5.8.tar.xz, expected SHA256 `58910198d19e873048fe87cdfe16bc790025417ede3d1651bfa1c4b533d573f2`, from retained Gate49 official release metadata. Verify before extraction; inspect archive member paths and reject absolute/traversal/symlink escapes or unexpected top-level roots. No archive is fetched here.

Resolve M4 PHP_SOURCE_ROOT=Q/source/php-8.5.8 and PHP_INSTALL_PREFIX=Q/php. Execute the unchanged M4 argv from the fresh Q/build directory only in a future authorized gate. M4 uses absolute source configure path and PHP metadata's separate abs_srcdir/builddir model; no source regeneration is allowed. The future generated Makefile must retain the exact prefix and build/source roots. Refuse a nonfresh config.cache/config.status. Compile once using `/usr/bin/make -j2` under the governed M4 clean environment; then `/usr/bin/make install` from Q/build, without sudo or DESTDIR/INSTALL_ROOT override. Preserve generated commands, exits and durations. Generated build tools must resolve within the build tree or qualified system tooling, not ambient PHP. Any failure ends the campaign with no retry.

## Configuration and runtime selection

Materialize Gate54's exact CANONICAL_PHP_INI_SPEC bytes, replacing only its root placeholder with canonical Q, after rejecting quotes/newlines/control characters. The four empty directives and sys_temp_dir remain unchanged. Create an empty owned scan directory; do not copy system ini or add extension/zend_extension lines. Runtime PHPRC=Q/configuration/php.ini and PHP_INI_SCAN_DIR=Q/configuration/empty-scan, with no empty-path/trailing-colon fallback.

For runtime commands set PATH=Q/composer/bin:Q/php/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, PHPRC and PHP_INI_SCAN_DIR as above, TMPDIR=Q/tmp, HOME=Q/home, COMPOSER_HOME=Q/composer-home and COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR=Q/composer-cache. Use a clean controlled environment with fixed locale/timezone; no LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, aliases, functions, BASH_ENV, ENV or PHP override flags. Reset shell command caching. Publish exact path/config bindings to subsequent qualification steps; each step rechecks them before execution. Do not serialize inherited secrets or environment dumps.

Before trusting `php`, require command resolution and realpath equal Q/php/bin/php. Invoke the exact executable directly for a nonzero-exit-checked JSON observation: PHP_BINARY realpath, PHP_VERSION exactly 8.5.8, PHP_SAPI=cli, executable hash, php_ini_loaded_file(), php_ini_scanned_files(), get_loaded_extensions(), ini_get('extension_dir'), required process functions and Gate54 configuration/temp probes. Reject absent, empty, malformed, extra-unexpected schema or mismatched observations. Discover extension_dir from the exact executable; do not invent its API directory. Record that no required shared extension exists; verify all 27 required extension_loaded results and all 21 STATIC/six BUILTIN expectations. Verify binary/system library resolution against M3; unresolved or unqualified dependencies fail. Default capabilities do not replace loaded-runtime evidence.

Run Gate54's PHP_BINARY child probe with the same environment and require matching binary/ini/scan/function/temp observations. The same inheritance contract applies to Composer and any later separately authorized test/release children; this specification does not execute Packaging.

## Composer and platform

Future artifact URL is https://getcomposer.org/download/2.9.4/composer.phar, expected SHA256 `d3eb5c4cb2e708267dac5f9a76d2a57b07836c7ea68783a1a02bd6d94753ea80`. Retain Gate49 independent metadata provenance. Download only to Q/downloads, verify before first invocation and promote atomically to Q/composer/composer-2.9.4.phar. Never execute an unverified PHAR.

The controlled wrapper's only execution is `exec "Q/php/bin/php" "Q/composer/composer-2.9.4.phar" "$@"`, with Q rendered safely once as quoted literal argv paths, not eval. Verify wrapper bytes and resolved path before use; verify artifact hash again before version/platform checks. Require exact normalized Composer version 2.9.4, nonzero/empty/malformed output fails. Ambient composer is never a fallback.

From the project checkout run exact PHP plus verified PHAR with `--no-plugins --no-scripts --no-interaction check-platform-reqs --lock --format=json`, including dev requirements. Require zero exit and each recovered requirement success; no install/update or network dependency resolution. Record input composer.json/composer.lock hashes before/after; no modifications permitted. Reject changed lock/platform authority. Child environment must bind Composer to the exact runtime; the wrapper and direct PHP invocation provide deterministic binding, not merely a declared expected version.

## Failure, evidence and cleanup

Every stage has one attempt, no fallback and no repair/retry. Before each stage verify prior PASS and invariant hashes. Preserve first failure, exit, bounded sanitized output and monotonic duration; downstream unexecuted stages remain NOT_EXECUTED. Capture successful identities, trust proofs, dependency transaction, configure/build/install exits, extension/configuration results and platform results. Do not claim runtime compatibility, Hosted success or duration fit from this document.

Keep bounded evidence under Q/evidence and publish it before cleanup in a separately authorized qualification mechanism. Never retain tokens, application .env, credentials, private keys or unfiltered environment. Preserve hashes/public provenance rather than raw key material. Logs must be sanitized and capped; truncation must be explicit. No release artifacts are uploaded as qualification evidence.

Cleanup occurs only after required evidence is safely preserved. Validate Q still equals the recorded canonical campaign-owned path beneath RUNNER_TEMP and remains disjoint from repository/system/output paths. Cleanup may remove only this campaign's temporary state; never follow symlinks or delete parent/shared roots. On evidence-preservation failure, retain state until ephemeral runner teardown and report the limitation. Cleanup errors do not overwrite the first qualification failure.

## Timing limitation

Measure monotonic durations separately for trust observation, apt refresh/package installation, source verification (and separately extraction), configure, compile, install, post-install PHP verification, Composer provisioning/verification, platform verification and total campaign. Preserve start/end timestamps and durations even on failure. The qualification is bounded by a 3600-second job deadline with no retry; timeout is a failure, never a speed estimate. Compile uses two workers as a bounded concurrency model, without changing M4 compiler flags or claiming release fit.

Actual durations remain UNRESOLVED. Retained release timeout is 3600 seconds, but Packaging B/upload and successful complete Packaging timings are unmeasured. After a future measurement, reconcile measured provisioning plus source-supported upper bounds for non-runtime release work and evidence/upload overhead against that timeout. If any required non-runtime bound is missing, report time fit UNRESOLVED and prohibit release-workflow adoption. Do not run Packaging to fill those gaps in the qualification campaign. A fit claim requires the complete sum strictly below the timeout; observed single-run timing alone is not an upper bound. Cache necessity remains UNRESOLVED pending measurement and complete release-time reconciliation. No cache is introduced here. These deliberately deferred observations do not invalidate static five-model closure.

## Future runtime negative guards

After real positive runtime observations, run six bounded isolated command-selection/observation fixtures: exact PHP and Composer succeeds; wrong PHP, wrong Composer, missing PHP, missing Composer and a missing required-extension observation each fail. Use fixture copies of observations or untrusted-path stubs in Q/tmp; never mutate the trusted installed binaries, configuration or source. Distinguish synthetic negative cases from real loaded-runtime evidence. Any negative case unexpectedly admitted fails the campaign. No tests/Packaging/release certification are performed by this runtime qualification specification.

Evidence limits are 1 MiB retained sanitized stdout and 1 MiB stderr per stage, plus 10 MiB structured evidence; exceeding them causes explicit evidence-incomplete failure, with bounded prefix/tail and full-stream hash where safely computable. Never overwrite the first runtime failure with a logging/cleanup failure. A future implementation must enforce the contract and its bounds before it is allowed to consume the single campaign. Readiness is a static design decision, not permission to dispatch or mutate Git.
